categories.title: Progression
categories.blurb: The tiers and the parts they are built from.

entries.name: Tiers
entries.summary: Every machine is built around a Machine Casing, and every casing is crafted around the one below it, so the tiers come in order.

blocks.html: Every machine is built around a Machine Casing, and every casing is crafted around the one below it, so the tiers come in order.

T0, by hand: Iron and Copper Plates, Iron Gears and Copper Wire, at double the cost the presses charge.
T1, Basic Casing: Plate Press, Gear Press, Wire Mill, Induction Smelter, Fuel Generator, Electric Furnace, Crusher, Washer, Sifter, Water and Wind Turbines, Geo Scanner.
T2, Steel Casing: the Induction Smelter makes Steel, Rose Gold and Redstone Alloy. Unlocks the Basic Quarry, Solar Panel, Redstone Dynamo, Item Vacuum, Mob Repeller, Assembler, Lava Pump, Magma Generator, Steel Crate and most chips.
T3, Hardened Casing: Hardened Steel from steel and Obsidian Dust. Unlocks the Reinforced Quarry, Purifier, Chunk Loader, Hardened Crate, Fortune, Silk Touch and Prospector chips.
T4, Deepcore Casing: Deepcore Alloy from Diamond Dust, Netherite Scrap and Hardened Steel. Unlocks the Deepcore Quarry and Deepcore Crate.
Machines you already placed keep working; only new crafts follow these recipes.

entries.name: Machine Casings
entries.summary: The tier key. Basic Casing goes in the middle of the first machines; each higher casing is crafted around the one below.

blocks.html: The tier key. Basic Casing goes in the middle of the first machines; each higher casing is crafted around the one below.

entries.name: Plates
entries.summary: Flat metal for casings and machines. The Plate Press makes 1 plate per ingot from iron, copper, steel, rose gold, hardened steel and deepcore alloy. Iron and copper plates can…

blocks.html: Flat metal for casings and machines. The Plate Press makes 1 plate per ingot from iron, copper, steel, rose gold, hardened steel and deepcore alloy. Iron and copper plates can also be made by hand, for 2 ingots each.

entries.name: Gears
entries.summary: The Gear Press makes 1 Iron Gear from 2 Iron Plates, or 1 Steel Gear from 4 Steel Plates. Iron Gears can also be made by hand, for twice the iron.

blocks.html: The Gear Press makes 1 Iron Gear from 2 Iron Plates, or 1 Steel Gear from 4 Steel Plates. Iron Gears can also be made by hand, for twice the iron.

entries.name: Wire and Coils
entries.summary: The Wire Mill makes 3 Copper Wire from 1 copper ingot (by hand it takes 3). Coils go into generators and the Induction Smelter.

blocks.html: The Wire Mill makes 3 Copper Wire from 1 copper ingot (by hand it takes 3). Coils go into generators and the Induction Smelter.

entries.name: Alloys
entries.summary: Made in the Induction Smelter, with the two ingredients in either slot.

blocks.html:
Made in the Induction Smelter, with the two ingredients in either slot.
• Steel Ingot: 1 iron ingot + 2 coal or charcoal, or 1 iron dust (any grade) + 1 coal or charcoal
• Rose Gold Ingot: 3 copper ingots + 1 gold ingot makes 4
• Redstone Alloy Ingot: 1 copper ingot + 4 redstone dust
• Hardened Steel Ingot: 1 steel ingot + 2 obsidian dust
• Deepcore Blend: 2 diamond dust + 1 netherite scrap
• Deepcore Alloy Ingot: 1 deepcore blend + 1 hardened steel ingot
Not crafted: Induction Smelter only.

entries.name: Obsidian and Diamond Dust
entries.summary: Made by the Crusher: 1 obsidian makes 2 Obsidian Dust, 1 diamond makes 1 Diamond Dust. Load them by hand or with a pipe. To keep a quarry line from grinding your diamonds, put…

blocks.html: Made by the Crusher: 1 obsidian makes 2 Obsidian Dust, 1 diamond makes 1 Diamond Dust. Load them by hand or with a pipe. To keep a quarry line from grinding your diamonds, put a Filter Upgrade on the pipe that feeds the Crusher.
Not crafted: Crusher only.

entries.name: Circuits
entries.summary: Go into chips, machines and quarries.

blocks.html: Go into chips, machines and quarries.

entries.name: Blank Chip
entries.summary: The base of every upgrade chip.

blocks.html: The base of every upgrade chip.

entries.name: Diamond Drill Head
entries.summary: Two go into the Basic Quarry Controller.

blocks.html: Two go into the Basic Quarry Controller.

entries.name: Deepcore Guide Book
entries.summary: This guide. Every player gets one when they first join.

blocks.html: This guide. Every player gets one when they first join.
Hold it and right-click. If you lose it, craft another.
Crafting table, any order: Book + Iron Ingot

entries.name: Water Turbine
entries.summary: The cheapest power and the best first one, day and night. Each side touching running water makes 0.25 power per tick (5 per second), up to 4 sides for 1 power per tick (20 per…

blocks.html: The cheapest power and the best first one, day and night. Each side touching running water makes 0.25 power per tick (5 per second), up to 4 sides for 1 power per tick (20 per second). Stores 1,000.

Place it so that running water touches it: flowing water, not a still pond or a source block. Put an Electric Furnace right against it (touching machines share power) or join them with Power Cables, and you can smelt without coal. More sides in the flow means more power, so wrap it in moving water on up to 4 sides. To make a stream, pour a water bucket on a slope and put the turbine in the moving part.

entries.name: Fuel Generator
entries.summary: Burns fuel for 8 power per tick. Stores 16,000.

blocks.html: Burns fuel for 8 power per tick. Stores 16,000.

Right-click it holding coal, charcoal, a coal block, a blaze rod, a dried kelp block or a lava bucket (sneak to load the whole stack). A pipe Output side facing it feeds it as well. Place it against a quarry or machine, or link with Power Cables.

entries.name: Redstone Dynamo
entries.summary: A stronger burner: 24 power per tick. Stores 48,000.

blocks.html: A stronger burner: 24 power per tick. Stores 48,000.
Loads like the Fuel Generator, but burns redstone dust (30 seconds each) or redstone blocks (4.5 minutes each).

entries.name: Magma Generator
entries.summary: Burns lava: 16 power a tick (320 a second), twice a Fuel Generator, for the same 160,000 power per bucket, so a bucket lasts 500 seconds and it holds 16. A Lava Pump keeping it…

blocks.html: Burns lava: 16 power a tick (320 a second), twice a Fuel Generator, for the same 160,000 power per bucket, so a bucket lasts 500 seconds and it holds 16. A Lava Pump keeping it fed draws 280 a second, so one generator and one pump only just pay for themselves: put two or more generators on a pump. Feed it from a touching Lava Pump, by hand, or with a pipe Output side carrying lava buckets. The empty buckets wait inside: a pipe Input side pulls them out, or right-click it with an empty hand.

entries.name: Solar Panel
entries.summary: Free power in daylight: up to 2 per tick at noon. Stores 6,000.

blocks.html: Free power in daylight: up to 2 per tick at noon. Stores 6,000.
Needs open sky. Night, a roof above it and thunder stop or cut it; rain cuts it a lot. Over a whole day it averages well under half its peak, so pair it with a battery.

entries.name: Wind Turbine
entries.summary: A tall tower with a three-blade rotor: up to 3 power per tick, day and night. Stores 8,000.

blocks.html: A tall tower with a three-blade rotor: up to 3 power per tick, day and night. Stores 8,000.

Place the black machine block with 8 free blocks straight above it; the tower and rotor build themselves and the rotor faces you. Connect cables or machines to the black block. Power depends on how high the rotor hub is: 30% at y=63 up to 100% from about y=183, so build on a hill. A roof above, blocks crowding the rotor, and calm weather cut it; storms add to it. Overworld only. Breaking the tower or the machine removes the whole turbine and gives back one Wind Turbine.

entries.name: Battery Banks
entries.summary: Store power for later. Seven tiers, each double the last: Stone 6,400, Copper 12,800, Iron 25,600, Gold 51,200, Redstone 102,400, Diamond 204,800, Netherite 409,600.

blocks.html: Store power for later. Seven tiers, each double the last: Stone 6,400, Copper 12,800, Iron 25,600, Gold 51,200, Redstone 102,400, Diamond 204,800, Netherite 409,600.

Put one in the network. It charges from the spare power of generators and panels and gives it back when they run dry. Bigger banks charge faster. Four bars on the block show its charge. Mine one and it keeps its charge: the item shows "Charge: ..." and placing it puts the power back (an explosion destroys the charge). Upgrade a bank by crafting it in the middle of the next tier's ring: 8 copper plates, 8 iron plates, 8 gold ingots, 8 redstone alloy ingots, diamonds with hardened steel plates, or netherite ingots with deepcore alloy plates.

entries.name: Creative Battery
entries.summary: Unlimited power that never runs out.

blocks.html: Unlimited power that never runs out.
Cannot be crafted. Get it from the creative inventory or with /give @s dq:creative_battery. Handy for testing.

entries.name: Power Cables
entries.summary: Link power machines, quarries and machines that are not touching. Six tiers with these limits in power per second: Copper 100, Iron 250, Gold 500, Redstone 1,000, Diamond…

blocks.html: Link power machines, quarries and machines that are not touching. Six tiers with these limits in power per second: Copper 100, Iron 250, Gold 500, Redstone 1,000, Diamond 2,000, Netherite 6,000.

Place cables between machines; they join each other and draw an arm toward what they connect to. Each cable only limits the power that goes through it: a run of one tier carries its rate, shared by everything drawing through that run, so a Copper cable feeding one machine off a Gold line limits that machine, not the Gold line. Machines touching a quarry are never limited. Only Copper cable is crafted from scratch: every other tier is made by upgrading the tier below with the next material (iron ingot, gold ingot, redstone alloy ingot, diamond, netherite ingot).

Put 8 cables of one tier in a ring around 1 dye in a crafting table to get 8 dyed ones. Undyed cables join anything, but dyed ones only join cables of the same color, so differently colored lines can run right next to each other. Use a stack of dyed cables on a water cauldron to wash the whole stack back to undyed (uses a little water).

Only Copper cable is crafted from scratch. Every other tier is an upgrade of the one below: craft one cable with one of the next material, in any order.
Copper + Iron Ingot = Iron
Iron + Gold Ingot = Gold
Gold + Redstone Alloy Ingot = Redstone
Redstone + Diamond = Diamond
Diamond + Netherite Ingot = Netherite

entries.name: Power Converter (UtilityCraft)
entries.summary: Links Deepcore power with UtilityCraft's Dorios Energy (DE), if UtilityCraft is installed in the same world. It moves up to 1,000 units per second. 1 unit = 5 DE, and 10% is…

blocks.html: Links Deepcore power with UtilityCraft's Dorios Energy (DE), if UtilityCraft is installed in the same world. It moves up to 1,000 units per second. 1 unit = 5 DE, and 10% is lost each way, so power cannot be looped between two converters for free. It holds 20,000 units.

Deepcore Power Cables and UtilityCraft energy cables both plug into any side (it can also just touch a UtilityCraft machine or a Deepcore power machine). Right-click it to choose a mode:
Import: UtilityCraft generators and batteries fill it like one of their machines, and the power joins the Deepcore network (batteries charge from it, quarries and machines draw from it).
Export: it takes power from the Deepcore network (generators first, then batteries) and adds DE to every UtilityCraft machine and battery on its cables.
Off: does nothing.
The lamp is blue on Import and orange on Export, the arrow shows which way power goes, and the bars show how full it is. Without UtilityCraft it stays idle and says why. A future UtilityCraft update could stop it working until Deepcore is updated; it then idles and nothing else is affected. Sneak + Pipe Wrench picks it up (the power inside is lost).

entries.name: Tesseract
entries.summary: Sends power and items to every other Tesseract on the same channel, in any dimension.

blocks.html: Sends power and items to every other Tesseract on the same channel, in any dimension.

Tap it with an empty hand and put a dye in each of the three left slots. Tesseracts with the same three dyes share a channel. Private (the default): only your own Tesseracts join. Public: anyone's Public Tesseracts with those dyes join.

Sneak + tap with an empty hand to pick Send, Receive or Off for power and for items, Public or Private, and a name. Only the player who placed it can change these.
• Power Send: takes power from its cables (generators first, batteries last) into the channel.
• Power Receive: fills its own 20,000 store from the channel; machines, batteries and a Power Converter on its cables draw from it. 5% is lost on the way, 10% from another dimension.
• Items Send: a pipe Output side facing it (or a machine next to it) puts items in its 9 slots and they go to the channel, for 5 power each, 10 to another dimension.
• Items Receive: items from the channel wait in its 9 slots for a pipe Input side to take them. Use pipe filters to sort.
• Chests, barrels, hoppers and shulker boxes touching it work without a pipe: a sending Tesseract empties them, a receiving one fills them (turn this off in its settings).
Only plain stackable items travel (no tools, enchanted or named things), like Deep Storage Crates.

Up to 50,000 power and 27 stacks wait on a channel, saved with the world. Each end works whenever its own chunk is loaded, so the other end can be unloaded. To keep a machine line in another dimension running while nobody is there, put a Chunk Loader next to it. When the buffer is full, senders wait. Breaking a Tesseract keeps its channel's buffer.

With no chips: 1,000 power and 16 items a second. Each Speed Chip adds that again, up to 6,000 power and 96 items (a Netherite cable and pipe) with 5 on a Deepcore Tesseract. Each Efficiency Chip cuts the loss and the item cost by 20%: 5 make it free. Machine Upgrades make it Steel, then Deepcore: 2 more chip slots each.

entries.name: Power Meter Block
entries.summary: A Power Meter you place, so you do not have to carry one. It always watches the network it is touching.

blocks.html: A Power Meter you place, so you do not have to carry one. It always watches the network it is touching.

Place it against a Power Cable, a power machine or a quarry (cables plug into its sides). The screen on the front shows how full the network's storage is (four bars) and a lamp: green when more power is made than used, red when the network is draining, yellow when it is steady. Look at it to see stored power, supply, draw and net per second on the action bar. Tap it with an empty hand for its live screen (it updates while open): a gauge, stored power, supply, draw, net, how long until full or empty and the cables, with a Supply tab and a Draw tab listing each kind of machine on the network, how many, and what they make or use. Holding an item, tap it to get a reminder instead. It reads the network but does not carry power, so it never links two networks. Sneak to build against it; sneak + Pipe Wrench picks it up.

entries.name: Power Meter
entries.summary: Shows a whole power network at a glance.

blocks.html: Shows a whole power network at a glance.
Right-click any power machine, cable or quarry with it: it lists stored power and capacity by machine type, power made per second, and which quarries are on the network.

categories.title: Big power
categories.blurb: The Core Reactor and the Induction Matrix.

entries.name: Core Reactor
entries.summary: The biggest generator: 800 to 8,000 power a second from Fuel Rods.

blocks.html: The biggest generator: 800 to 8,000 power a second from Fuel Rods.

A hollow box, 5 x 5 x 5 up to 9 x 9 x 9 on the outside. Every outside block is Reactor Casing, except: one Reactor Controller, at least one Reactor Fuel Port, and Reactor Glass anywhere in the middle of a face (not on edges or corners). Inside: air and water source blocks only. Tap the controller: it says whether it is formed, and if not, why (a gap, glass on an edge, something inside).

Feed Fuel Rods into a fuel port (by hand or with a pipe); it holds 4, and one rod is 20,000,000 power. Tap the controller, press Start and set the burn rate (10-100%): each % is 80 power a second, and heat is a twentieth of the power. Cable the controller to your network.

It cools 10 a second by itself, plus 4 a second for every water source block inside, so a bigger reactor full of water runs hotter safely. Coolant fed into a fuel port (Ice 40, Packed Ice 360, Blue Ice 3,240, Snow Block 20) soaks up heat while it lasts. 500 heat: warning. 800: danger, alarm. 1,000: meltdown. A redstone signal on the controller stops it at once.
What a meltdown does is up to the server: /scriptevent dq:meltdown off (it just stops at 999), contained (the default: the fuel is lost and the inside burns) or full (it explodes).
If the buffer is full it waits, burning nothing. Mining the controller gives back whole Fuel Rods.

entries.name: Fuel Rod
entries.summary: Core Reactor fuel: 20,000,000 power, about 42 minutes at full burn.

blocks.html: Core Reactor fuel: 20,000,000 power, about 42 minutes at full burn.

1: Hardened Steel Plate | Blaze Rod | Hardened Steel Plate
2: Hardened Steel Plate | Deepcore Blend | Hardened Steel Plate
3: Hardened Steel Plate | Blaze Rod | Hardened Steel Plate

Reactor Casing (makes 4): Hardened Steel Plate in the corners, Steel Plate on the sides, middle empty.
Reactor Glass (makes 4): Glass in the middle, Reactor Casing above, below, left and right.
Reactor Controller: Reactor Casing in the corners, Elite Circuit top and bottom, Advanced Circuit left and right, Deepcore Machine Casing in the middle.
Reactor Fuel Port: Reactor Casing in the corners, Hoppers on the sides, middle empty.

entries.name: Induction Matrix
entries.summary: A huge battery: from 2,000,000 to hundreds of millions of power.

blocks.html: A huge battery: from 2,000,000 to hundreds of millions of power.

A hollow box, 3 x 3 x 3 up to 9 x 9 x 9 on the outside. Every outside block is Matrix Casing, Matrix Glass (middle of a face only) or a Matrix Port. Inside: Matrix Cells (Steel 2,000,000, Deepcore 8,000,000), Matrix Providers and air. It needs at least one cell and one port.

Cable each port to a network and tap it to set it: Input takes power in, Output gives power out. Each port moves 4,000 a second, plus 4,000 for every Provider inside. The glass glows brighter the fuller it is, and the Power Meter shows what it holds.
The power belongs to the structure, not the ports, so you can move ports. Breaking cells makes it smaller: power above the new size is lost.

Matrix Casing (makes 4): Steel Plate in the corners, Lapis Lazuli on the sides.
Matrix Glass (makes 4): Glass in the middle, Matrix Casing around it (4).
Matrix Port: Matrix Casing in the corners, Advanced Circuit top and bottom, Redstone Coil left and right, Steel Machine Casing in the middle.
Steel Matrix Cell: Steel Plate in the corners, Diamond Battery Bank on the sides, Advanced Circuit in the middle.
Deepcore Matrix Cell: Deepcore Alloy Plate in the corners, Steel Matrix Cell on the sides, Elite Circuit in the middle.
Matrix Provider: Steel Plate in the corners, Redstone Coil on the sides, Elite Circuit in the middle.

categories.title: Machines
categories.blurb: These use power from the same network as the quarry.

entries.name: Machine screens
entries.summary: Tap a machine with an empty hand to open its screen, like a chest: put items in, take results out, and open the chips tab (the chip on the right edge) to install Speed,…

blocks.html: Tap a machine with an empty hand to open its screen, like a chest: put items in, take results out, and open the chips tab (the chip on the right edge) to install Speed, Efficiency and other chips: a chip dropped in the wrong chip slot moves to its own. The i tab explains how the machine works. Shift-click works. The arrow shows progress and the dark panel shows what it is doing, its speed, its power cost and the power on the network. The first tap after you look at a machine can just put the screen up: tap again.

Settings: sneak and tap with an empty hand. The Assembler asks for a recipe; the Item Vacuum, Chunk Loader and Mob Repeller set their radius and on/off; the Lava Pump starts and stops; quarry controllers open their menu (Start, Stop, area, statistics, Void Filter list).

Screens: Electric Furnace, Crusher, Plate Press, Gear Press, Wire Mill, Induction Smelter, Washer, Purifier, Sifter, Assembler, Item Vacuum, Chunk Loader, Mob Repeller, Lava Pump (put empty buckets in, take lava buckets out), Fuel Generator, Redstone Dynamo, Magma Generator (fuel goes straight into its store; empty buckets wait in a slot) and the quarry controllers (chips and the items waiting for room at the outputs). Geo Scanners work as before; crates show their item on the front (see Deep Storage Crates). Item pipes have a filter screen too (see Filter Upgrade).
Hold a block and sneak to place it against a machine. To mine one, just keep hitting it: the screen steps aside.
Furnaces, the Crusher, the presses, the Induction Smelter and the Assembler also have an On demand tab: see On demand machines.

entries.name: Machine tiers
entries.summary: Every machine that takes chips is Basic when you place it. Use a Steel Machine Upgrade on it (hold it and tap the machine) to make it Steel, then a Deepcore Machine Upgrade to…

blocks.html:
Every machine that takes chips is Basic when you place it. Use a Steel Machine Upgrade on it (hold it and tap the machine) to make it Steel, then a Deepcore Machine Upgrade to make it Deepcore. Tiers go in order: a Deepcore Upgrade on a Basic machine is refused. Each tier adds 2 chip slots:
• Electric Furnace, Crusher, Plate Press, Gear Press, Wire Mill, Induction Smelter, Washer, Purifier, Sifter, Assembler: Speed and Efficiency up to 3 each (Basic, 6 slots), 4 each (Steel, 8), 5 each (Deepcore, 10). 4 Speed Chips work 5x as fast, 5 work 6x.
• Item Vacuum, Chunk Loader, Mob Repeller, Lava Pump: Efficiency up to 3, 4, 5, and from Steel they take Range Chips (1 at Steel, 2 at Deepcore): Vacuum radius +4 blocks each, Repeller radius +8, Chunk Loader one more ring of chunks (up to 11x11), Lava Pump reach +4.

The dark panel on the machine's screen shows its tier and chips in use. A Steel machine has blue trim and a Deepcore one teal trim, and it keeps its tier when you mine or wrench it: it drops as a Steel or Deepcore item that places as that tier, with its chips coming back out as usual. The Tesseract takes Machine Upgrades too: a Steel one has deep blue edges and smoky glass, a Deepcore one teal edges and teal glass. Quarry controllers keep their own tiers (Basic, Reinforced, Deepcore), and generators take no chips, so neither takes Machine Upgrades.

entries.name: On demand machines
entries.summary: The Electric Furnace, Crusher, Plate Press, Gear Press, Wire Mill, Induction Smelter and Assembler have an On demand tab on their screen (the tab with the chest). Tap the lever…

blocks.html: The Electric Furnace, Crusher, Plate Press, Gear Press, Wire Mill, Induction Smelter and Assembler have an On demand tab on their screen (the tab with the chest). Tap the lever to switch it on or off.

Off (how machines always worked): it takes everything pipes bring and works until its output slot is full.
On: it looks at where its output goes and only takes the inputs for what is still wanted there, then waits. Nothing piles up inside it, so one machine can make several things (a Gear Press can make Iron and Steel Gears).

• a pipe Output side with a Stock Upgrade: what is missing up to its number
• a chest, barrel or hopper without one: whatever fits (so use a Stock Upgrade)
• another On demand machine: what it needs for its own output, so chains work

While it waits its status starts with On demand. Anything still in its inputs then (loaded by hand, something it cannot use, or a few left over) is sent on like its results: into a touching chest, or a touching pipe whose side toward it is Input or Output, so a stray item never clogs the line. See Keeping a chest stocked for a full example.

entries.name: Deepcore Crafting Table
entries.summary: A crafting table with a recipe book that shows the way. Tap it with an empty hand (no power needed); the first tap can just put the screen up: tap again.

blocks.html: A crafting table with a recipe book that shows the way. Tap it with an empty hand (no power needed); the first tap can just put the screen up: tap again.

Recipe book (left)
Tabs: All, Deepcore, Craftable now and Search (type a name; the screen closes, tap the table again for the results). Arrows turn the pages. Recipes you cannot make yet are red. Tap one to put it in the grid; tap it again for its next recipe.

Grid (right)
The recipe's ingredients, red where you are missing them. Tap a red one and its own recipe goes in the grid; the back arrow returns to the recipe you came from. Items with no crafting recipe show what they come from (a furnace, a stonecutter, a Deepcore machine). Take the result to craft one; the stack button crafts as many as fit in a stack; the red X clears the grid. You can also lay real items in the grid like a normal crafting table; they come back to you when you look away.

It counts and crafts from your inventory plus one chest or barrel touching it (a double chest counts as one). It takes from you first, then the chest. Results go to you; if you are full, into the chest; if that is full too, they drop on the table.

entries.name: Steel Machine Upgrade
entries.summary: Raises a Basic machine to Steel: 2 more chip slots. See Machine tiers.

blocks.html: Raises a Basic machine to Steel: 2 more chip slots. See Machine tiers.
Hold it and tap the machine. It is used up, and the machine keeps its new tier when mined.

entries.name: Deepcore Machine Upgrade
entries.summary: Raises a Steel machine to Deepcore: 2 more chip slots. See Machine tiers.

blocks.html: Raises a Steel machine to Deepcore: 2 more chip slots. See Machine tiers.
Hold it and tap the machine. It is used up, and the machine keeps its new tier when mined.

entries.name: Plate Press
entries.summary: Presses ingots into plates. Uses 200 power per item and takes 6 seconds (Speed Chips make it faster).

blocks.html: Presses ingots into plates. Uses 200 power per item and takes 6 seconds (Speed Chips make it faster).

1 ingot of iron, copper, steel, rose gold, hardened steel or deepcore alloy makes 1 plate (half the iron of the hand recipe). Load it by right-clicking with an item (sneak for the stack) or with pipes. Metal Presses placed before 4.0.4 are Plate Presses now; one that was set to Gears, Wire or Dust turned into a Gear Press, Wire Mill or Crusher.

entries.name: Gear Press
entries.summary: Presses plates into gears. Uses 200 power per item and takes 6 seconds (Speed Chips make it faster).

blocks.html: Presses plates into gears. Uses 200 power per item and takes 6 seconds (Speed Chips make it faster).
2 Iron Plates make 1 Iron Gear (half the iron of the hand recipe). 4 Steel Plates make 1 Steel Gear. Load it by right-clicking with an item (sneak for the stack) or with pipes.

entries.name: Wire Mill
entries.summary: Draws copper into wire. Uses 200 power per item and takes 6 seconds (Speed Chips make it faster).

blocks.html: Draws copper into wire. Uses 200 power per item and takes 6 seconds (Speed Chips make it faster).
1 copper ingot makes 3 Copper Wire (by hand it takes 3 ingots). Load it by right-clicking with an item (sneak for the stack) or with pipes.

entries.name: Induction Smelter
entries.summary: Mixes two ingredients into alloys (see Alloys under Crafting parts), and smelts raw iron, gold and copper with a 25% chance of a second ingot. Uses 600 power per alloy and…

blocks.html: Mixes two ingredients into alloys (see Alloys under Crafting parts), and smelts raw iron, gold and copper with a 25% chance of a second ingot. Uses 600 power per alloy and takes 10 seconds when hot.

It has two input slots and puts each item where it fits, so pipes can feed both ingredients down one line. It starts at 25% speed and heats up to full speed over 30 seconds of steady work, and cools when it stops, so give it steady power. Right-click with an item to load it (sneak for the stack).

entries.name: Electric Furnace
entries.summary: Smelts ores, raw metals, dusts, sand, cobblestone, food and logs with no fuel. One item every 8 seconds, down to 2 seconds with 3 Speed Chips.

blocks.html: Smelts ores, raw metals, dusts, sand, cobblestone, food and logs with no fuel. One item every 8 seconds, down to 2 seconds with 3 Speed Chips.

Touch it to a power machine (a Water Turbine is a good first one) or link it with cables. Load it by right-click (sneak for a whole stack) or with a pipe Output side. It pushes results into a touching chest, or into a touching pipe whose side toward it is set to Input or Output.

entries.name: Crusher
entries.summary: Crushes ore or raw metal into 2 dust (lapis and redstone give 8 to 10). Also cobblestone to gravel, gravel to sand, bones to bone meal, obsidian to 2 Obsidian Dust and diamond…

blocks.html: Crushes ore or raw metal into 2 dust (lapis and redstone give 8 to 10). Also cobblestone to gravel, gravel to sand, bones to bone meal, obsidian to 2 Obsidian Dust and diamond to Diamond Dust. The only machine that can turn ore into dust.

Powered and loaded like the Electric Furnace. One item every 8 seconds, down to 2 with Speed Chips. Pipes feed it anything it can crush, diamonds and obsidian included: filter the pipe if you want to keep those.

entries.name: Item Vacuum
entries.summary: Pulls loose items within a radius of 2 to 16 blocks into its output.

blocks.html: Pulls loose items within a radius of 2 to 16 blocks into its output.
Give it power and a chest or pipe to send items to. A bigger radius costs more power.

entries.name: Chunk Loader
entries.summary: Keeps the chunks around it loaded (3x3, 5x5 or 7x7) so quarries and machines keep working while you are away.

blocks.html: Keeps the chunks around it loaded (3x3, 5x5 or 7x7) so quarries and machines keep working while you are away.
Costs power per chunk and loaded chunks add lag. Limited to 2 per player.

entries.name: Mob Repeller
entries.summary: Stops hostile mobs from spawning within a radius of 4 to 32 blocks.

blocks.html: Stops hostile mobs from spawning within a radius of 4 to 32 blocks.
Needs power: bigger radius costs more, and with no power it does nothing.

entries.name: Assembler
entries.summary: Crafts DeepCore parts, machines, pipes and chips on its own. Sneak and tap it with an empty hand to choose a recipe; it then takes only the ingredients that recipe uses, from…

blocks.html: Crafts DeepCore parts, machines, pipes and chips on its own. Sneak and tap it with an empty hand to choose a recipe; it then takes only the ingredients that recipe uses, from your hand (sneak for the stack) or from pipe Output sides, so a mixed line never jams it. One craft every 10 seconds for 400 power (Speed and Efficiency Chips work). Results go to six output slots that pipes pull from, or push into a touching chest. It uses the same ingredients as the crafting table. Changing the recipe moves ingredients the new one does not use into the output.

Recipe grid (grid tab): lay out any crafting recipe. Put an item in a cell: it comes back to you and the cell keeps a picture. Then tap empty cells to copy that item into them (three taps of iron make a bucket). Take a picture out to clear its cell.
On demand (chest tab): switched on, it only takes ingredients for what a Stock Upgrade further down its pipes still wants. See On demand machines.

entries.name: Geo Scanner
entries.summary: Counts the ore under it before you place a quarry. Press Scan in its menu: for 2,000 power it reads its chunk from just below itself down to the bottom of the world and lists…

blocks.html: Counts the ore under it before you place a quarry. Press Scan in its menu: for 2,000 power it reads its chunk from just below itself down to the bottom of the world and lists every ore by kind, with the 16-block layer where each is richest. Stone and deepslate ore count together. Each Range Chip (up to 2) adds a ring of chunks: 3x3, then 5x5. Chunks that are not loaded are skipped, so stay nearby.

Hologram (4.25)
After a scan, press Show hologram: for 30 seconds a small model of the scanned area floats over the scanner, every ore spot a dot in its colour (diamond cyan, gold yellow, redstone red, iron tan, coal dark...), the surface at the top and the bottom of the world at the bottom. Scans are not kept over a server restart, so scan again then.

entries.name: Lava Pump
entries.summary: Drains lava. Every 2 minutes it takes the nearest lava source block within 8 blocks below or level with it, fills the hole with netherrack in the Nether or dirt elsewhere, and…

blocks.html: Drains lava. Every 2 minutes it takes the nearest lava source block within 8 blocks below or level with it, fills the hole with netherrack in the Nether or dirt elsewhere, and stores it in a 16-bucket tank. It draws 280 power a second the whole time it runs, even with a full tank (none when no lava is in reach), so it pays off with two or more Magma Generators: it keeps up to four fed. Flowing lava is never taken, so a lava fall cannot pump forever. It feeds every Magma Generator it touches straight from the tank. Right-click it with an empty bucket to fill the bucket. Efficiency Chips cut its power use. Its window shows how full the tank is.

entries.name: Deep Storage Crates
entries.summary: Hold thousands of one item: Steel 8,192, Hardened 32,768, Deepcore 131,072. The front shows a picture of the item it holds and how many (2.1k = 2,100). Right-click with an item…

blocks.html: Hold thousands of one item: Steel 8,192, Hardened 32,768, Deepcore 131,072. The front shows a picture of the item it holds and how many (2.1k = 2,100). Right-click with an item to store the stack, sneak to store all of that item you carry; right-click with an empty hand stores all of the crate's item you carry. Left-click takes a stack out. Sneak with an empty hand and right-click for the menu (take all, lock to the item). To break a crate, sneak while you mine it. Pipes push in and pull out like a chest. Only plain stackable items fit (no tools or named items). Mined or picked up with the wrench, a crate keeps what it holds, written on the item. Use a Hardened Casing on a Steel Crate, or a Deepcore Casing on a Hardened one, to upgrade it in place with its contents. The strip at the top of the front shows how full it is.
Crates can be joined into a Crate Network with a Crate Link (see Crate Network).

entries.name: Factory lanes
entries.summary: A Steel Electric Furnace, Crusher, Plate Press, Gear Press, Wire Mill, Washer, Purifier or Sifter works 3 stacks side by side; a Deepcore one works 5. A Basic machine has one…

blocks.html: A Steel Electric Furnace, Crusher, Plate Press, Gear Press, Wire Mill, Washer, Purifier or Sifter works 3 stacks side by side; a Deepcore one works 5. A Basic machine has one lane, as before.

Nothing to set up. Pipes spread what they bring over the open lanes, and pull every lane's output. On the machine's screen, the Lanes tab (three arrows) shows lanes 2 to 5 with their own input, progress arrow and output (Washers, Purifiers and Sifters share their six output slots and the Purifier's catalyst). A lane the tier has not opened is closed: its slots are hatched and a lock sits where its arrow would be. Each lane pays its own power, so a Deepcore machine with 5 busy lanes uses 5 times the power, and it shows how many lanes are busy in its status.
The Induction Smelter and Assembler keep one lane.

Steel and Deepcore ore machines also give more: a Steel Purifier has a 50% bonus dust chance (Basic 33%), a Deepcore Washer 67% (Basic 50%) and a Deepcore Purifier 50%. Crusher, Washer and Purifier together give about 4x the metal at Basic, 4.5x with a Steel Purifier and 5x with Deepcore Washer and Purifier.

categories.title: Ore processing
categories.blurb: Crusher, Washer, Purifier, Furnace: about 4 ingots per ore instead of 1.

entries.name: Washer
entries.summary: Turns dust into Clean Dust: 1.5 per dust on average, and 1 time in 10 a Slag as well.

blocks.html: Turns dust into Clean Dust: 1.5 per dust on average, and 1 time in 10 a Slag as well.
It takes dust only, never ore or raw metal: send those through the Crusher first. It must touch a water source block (still water, not flowing). Powered and loaded like the Crusher.
A Deepcore Washer has a 67% chance of the second Clean Dust (Basic and Steel 50%). Steel and Deepcore Washers have 3 and 5 lanes.

entries.name: Purifier
entries.summary: Turns Clean Dust into Pure Dust (1.33 per clean dust on average, with an 8% byproduct: iron gives coal, copper lapis, gold quartz). Also turns gem ore (coal, diamond, emerald,…

blocks.html: Turns Clean Dust into Pure Dust (1.33 per clean dust on average, with an 8% byproduct: iron gives coal, copper lapis, gold quartz). Also turns gem ore (coal, diamond, emerald, lapis, redstone, quartz) into about 1.5 times the Crusher's yield.
It burns a catalyst: right-click it with redstone dust or pipe it in. One redstone covers 8 items. Finished gems are refused. A Silk Touch quarry delivers whole gem ores.
Steel and Deepcore Purifiers have a 50% chance of the second Pure Dust (Basic 33%), and 3 and 5 lanes.

entries.name: Sifter
entries.summary: Gravel, sand, red sand, soul sand and Slag give small chances of flint, clay, bones, nuggets and rare gems.

blocks.html: Gravel, sand, red sand, soul sand and Slag give small chances of flint, clay, bones, nuggets and rare gems.
Powered and loaded like the Crusher.

categories.title: Quarry
categories.blurb: The digger and what controls it.

entries.name: Quarry Controllers
entries.summary: Digs a hole one layer at a time from just below itself to bedrock. Bigger controllers dig bigger areas: Basic up to 12 x 12 with 3 chip slots and 2 blocks a second, Reinforced…

blocks.html: Digs a hole one layer at a time from just below itself to bedrock. Bigger controllers dig bigger areas: Basic up to 12 x 12 with 3 chip slots and 2 blocks a second, Reinforced up to 24 x 24 with 6 slots and 4 a second, Deepcore up to 36 x 36 with 10 slots and 6 a second (more with Speed Chips). Range Chips add 4 to the size, up to 48 x 48.

Place it on the edge of the dig area. Give it an output (a chest, barrel or hopper touching it, or a pipe network), power (a machine touching it or cables) and right-click it to press Start. The default dig area is 9x9 in the direction you faced. Quarries need a lot of power: Basic on stone uses about 13 per tick. Stay nearby: it only works in loaded chunks.

entries.name: Boundary Marker
entries.summary: Sets the dig area. Crafting gives 3, which is the number you need.

blocks.html: Sets the dig area. Crafting gives 3, which is the number you need.

Use three. Place them at the same height in an L: a corner marker, one marker along the X axis from it and one along the Z axis from it. Right-click any of them and a red line is drawn between the three, showing the rectangle. Then place the quarry against the corner marker, the one in line with the other two. It works on the inside of the red line and leaves the markers where they are. The biggest area depends on the controller: Basic 12 x 12, Reinforced 24 x 24, Deepcore 36 x 36, plus 4 per Range Chip. With a marker touching the controller but fewer than 3 in an L, the quarry will not start.

categories.title: Chips
categories.blurb: Upgrades you right-click into a controller or machine.

entries.name: Speed Chip
entries.summary: Up to 3 (4 in a Steel machine, 5 in a Deepcore one). Quarries dig more blocks per cycle; furnaces, crushers and other machines work faster. Costs more power per block or item.

blocks.html: Up to 3 (4 in a Steel machine, 5 in a Deepcore one). Quarries dig more blocks per cycle; furnaces, crushers and other machines work faster. Costs more power per block or item.
Hold it and right-click the controller or machine. Each chip uses a chip slot. Chips come back out if you break the machine, or take them out of its screen.

entries.name: Efficiency Chip
entries.summary: Up to 3 (4 in a Steel machine, 5 in a Deepcore one). Each cuts power use by 15%, on quarries and on every machine.

blocks.html: Up to 3 (4 in a Steel machine, 5 in a Deepcore one). Each cuts power use by 15%, on quarries and on every machine.
Hold it and right-click the controller or machine.

entries.name: Range Chip
entries.summary: Up to 3. The largest dig area grows by 4 blocks per chip (up to 48 x 48). Steel and Deepcore Item Vacuums, Mob Repellers, Chunk Loaders and Lava Pumps take 1 or 2 (see Machine…

blocks.html: Up to 3. The largest dig area grows by 4 blocks per chip (up to 48 x 48). Steel and Deepcore Item Vacuums, Mob Repellers, Chunk Loaders and Lava Pumps take 1 or 2 (see Machine tiers): a bigger radius or reach.
Hold it and right-click the controller or machine, or drop it in the machine's chips tab.

entries.name: Fortune Chip
entries.summary: Up to 3. Ores give more, like the enchantment. Costs 25% more power per level.

blocks.html: Up to 3. Ores give more, like the enchantment. Costs 25% more power per level.
Quarry controllers only. Cannot be combined with Silk Touch.

entries.name: Silk Touch Chip
entries.summary: Ores, stone, glass, ice and similar come out whole. Costs 25% more power.

blocks.html: Ores, stone, glass, ice and similar come out whole. Costs 25% more power.
Quarry controllers only. Cannot be combined with Fortune. Use it to bring whole gem ores to the Purifier.

entries.name: Void Filter Chip
entries.summary: Throws away unwanted drops.

blocks.html: Throws away unwanted drops.
Install it, then set a list of up to 9 items in the controller menu: matching drops are deleted instead of sent to the output.

entries.name: Backfill Chip
entries.summary: Every block the quarry mines is replaced with dirt, so the hole fills in as it digs. Costs 10% more power.

blocks.html: Every block the quarry mines is replaced with dirt, so the hole fills in as it digs. Costs 10% more power.
Quarry controllers only. Handy to keep the ground level: nothing is left open to fall into, and water and lava cannot flow into the pit.

entries.name: Magnet Chip
entries.summary: Also collects loose items within 8 blocks of the controller.

blocks.html: Also collects loose items within 8 blocks of the controller.
Quarry controllers only.

entries.name: Prospector Chip
entries.summary: Quarries only. The quarry digs ore and ancient debris and leaves everything else standing, moving through stone 8 times faster. Ore costs 3 times the power. It cannot be…

blocks.html: Quarries only. The quarry digs ore and ancient debris and leaves everything else standing, moving through stone 8 times faster. Ore costs 3 times the power. It cannot be combined with Backfill.
Crafting table, any order: Blank Chip + Advanced Circuit + Hardened Steel Plate + Compass + Emerald

entries.name: Item Pipes
entries.summary: Carry items between chests, machines and quarries. Eight tiers, in items per second: Wooden 2, Stone 4, Copper 8, Iron 12, Gold 20, Redstone 32, Diamond 48, Netherite 96.

blocks.html: Carry items between chests, machines and quarries. Eight tiers, in items per second: Wooden 2, Stone 4, Copper 8, Iron 12, Gold 20, Redstone 32, Diamond 48, Netherite 96.

Pipes link to each other and to anything with an inventory, and draw an arm or flange toward it. A network is as fast as its slowest pipe and the speed is shared by everything on it. Set what each side does with the Pipe Wrench.

Put 8 pipes of one tier in a ring around 1 dye in a crafting table to get 8 dyed ones. Undyed pipes join anything, but dyed ones only join pipes of the same color, so differently colored lines can run right next to each other. Use a stack of dyed pipes on a water cauldron to wash the whole stack back to undyed (uses a little water).

Only Wooden pipes are crafted from scratch (2 planks of any wood with 1 glass between them, makes 2). Every other tier is an upgrade of the one below: craft one pipe with one of the next material, in any order.
Wooden + Cobblestone, Blackstone or Cobbled Deepslate = Stone
Stone + Copper Ingot = Copper
Copper + Iron Ingot = Iron
Iron + Gold Ingot = Gold
Gold + Redstone Block = Redstone
Redstone + Diamond = Diamond
Diamond + Netherite Ingot = Netherite

entries.name: Pipe Wrench
entries.summary: Sets what each side of a pipe does.

blocks.html: Sets what each side of a pipe does.

Right-click a pipe's side (or the side of the chest or machine it touches). Choose Disabled, Input (pull items out of the container) or Output (push items from the network into it). Outputs have a priority (High fills first) and a round robin option to share evenly. The filter has its own screen: tap the pipe with an empty hand (see Filter Upgrade).

A side only reaches its block once it is set: a Disabled side draws no arm, and a machine never pushes its results into it. Input sides get a blue sleeve behind the flange, Output sides an orange one; cyan teeth on the sleeve mean the side has a filter.

Sneak and right-click any machine, pipe, cable or boundary marker to pick it up (stored items, chips and fuel come back; a running quarry must be stopped first, and the Creative Battery cannot be picked up).

On a machine face with no pipe, the wrench sets that machine side (Both, In only, Out only, Closed) or, on the front, turns the machine. Used in the air, it opens the settings of what you wear (Jetpack hover, Mining Suit modules). See Gear: Machine sides.

entries.name: Filter Upgrade
entries.summary: Lets one pipe side move only chosen items.

blocks.html: Lets one pipe side move only chosen items.

Tap the pipe, or its flange where it sits on the chest or machine, with an empty hand to open its filter screen (the first tap can just put the screen up: tap again). The top row is the filter: put any item in a slot and it is copied as a ghost, while the real item goes straight back to you. Take a ghost out to remove it. The buttons below add or remove a whole category: Ores, Raw metals and dusts, Ore drops, Stone family, Dirt sand and gravel, Wood, Raw food, Cooked food, Ingots and DeepCore (every item and block from this add-on). Up to 9 entries.
• Allow list (green tick): the side moves only what is in the filter. Block list (red cross): everything except it. An empty filter moves everything.
• Side button: a pipe touching several containers has a filter for each side; tap it to switch. The panel shows the side, its mode and the filter size.
• The first change uses a Filter Upgrade from your inventory. To take it back out, use the Pipe Wrench on the side; breaking the pipe gives it back too.

entries.name: Stock Upgrade
entries.summary: Makes a pipe Output side keep only so many of each item in what it feeds, then stop, so one line can feed several machines without flooding the first. Carry one and use the…

blocks.html: Makes a pipe Output side keep only so many of each item in what it feeds, then stop, so one line can feed several machines without flooding the first. Carry one and use the Pipe Wrench on the side: type how many to keep (up to 1,728) and the upgrade goes in. It counts what the destination already holds: a chest's slots, a machine's input, a crate, or a generator's fuel. Works with or without a Filter Upgrade. Breaking the pipe gives it back. With On demand machines it keeps a chest topped up: see Keeping a chest stocked.
Crafting table, any order: Filter Upgrade + Comparator + Iron Plate

entries.name: Keeping a chest stocked
entries.summary: Example: always keep 16 Iron Gears and 16 Steel Gears in a chest, made from whatever is in your storage.

blocks.html: Example: always keep 16 Iron Gears and 16 Steel Gears in a chest, made from whatever is in your storage.

1. Storage: put a pipe on your storage chest and wrench that side to Input.
2. Machines: run the pipe past a Gear Press and wrench the side facing it to Output. Open the press, go to the On demand tab and switch it On.
3. Gear chest: run the pipe to the chest that should hold the gears. Wrench that side to Output and install a Stock Upgrade set to 16. A Filter Upgrade set to the gears stops plates going in.
Now when the chest has fewer than 16 of a gear, the press takes just enough plates to make the difference and stops again.

Plates from ingots too: add a Plate Press on the same pipe (Output side facing it), also On demand. When the Gear Press needs plates that storage does not have, the Plate Press takes the ingots for them. An On demand Induction Smelter can make the Steel Ingots before that.

• Don't let the gear chest touch a machine: a machine pushes straight into a chest it touches, with no limit.
• An Output side with no Stock Upgrade counts as wanting everything that fits.
• It works for anything these machines make: plates, wire, ingots, dusts.

entries.name: Crate Network
entries.summary: Joins your Deep Storage Crates into one store you can reach from a Network Terminal or a Portable Terminal.

blocks.html: Joins your Deep Storage Crates into one store you can reach from a Network Terminal or a Portable Terminal.

1. Place a Network Core and cable it to power (10 power a second, plus 1 for each crate).
2. Tap the core with a Crate Link. The link now knows that core.
3. Tap crates with the link to join them (tap again to take one out). Sneak + tap a crate joins every crate touching it, crate to crate, so a wall of crates joins in one tap.
4. Place a Network Terminal and tap it with the link too.
Crates can be anywhere in the core's dimension, loaded or not. Breaking the core frees its crates (they keep their items).

entries.name: Network Terminal
entries.summary: The Crate Network in a chest screen. Tap it with an empty hand. It shows 45 kinds of item per page, most first; take a stack out, or drop items onto it to store them (they go…

blocks.html:
The Crate Network in a chest screen. Tap it with an empty hand. It shows 45 kinds of item per page, most first; take a stack out, or drop items onto it to store them (they go into crates holding that item, then into empty crates).
Deposit puts everything in your inventory (not the hotbar) that the network already holds.
Sneak + tap with an empty hand to search or sort by name; the search button clears it.
Pipes use a terminal like a chest: an Output side facing it stores items in the network, and an Input side (with a filter) pulls them out, so one terminal can feed a whole factory.

1: Steel Plate | Glass Pane | Steel Plate
2: Basic Circuit | Chest | Basic Circuit
3: Steel Plate | Steel Plate | Steel Plate

entries.name: Network Core
entries.summary: The heart of a Crate Network. It needs power: 10 a second plus 1 for each crate. Without power the network is offline (the crates still work on their own). Tap it to see how…

blocks.html: The heart of a Crate Network. It needs power: 10 a second plus 1 for each crate. Without power the network is offline (the crates still work on their own). Tap it to see how many crates and items it has.

1: Steel Plate | Advanced Circuit | Steel Plate
2: Ender Pearl | Chest | Ender Pearl
3: Steel Plate | Steel Machine Casing | Steel Plate

entries.name: Crate Link
entries.summary: Tap a Network Core to set it, then tap crates and terminals to join them to that core (or take them out). Sneak + tap a crate: every crate touching it joins.

blocks.html: Tap a Network Core to set it, then tap crates and terminals to join them to that core (or take them out). Sneak + tap a crate: every crate touching it joins.
Crafting table, one column: Ender Pearl, Redstone Dust, Steel Plate

entries.name: Portable Terminal
entries.summary: The Network Terminal in your hand. Tap a Network Core with it, then use it anywhere in that dimension: search, take items, or deposit your inventory. The Deepcore Portable…

blocks.html: The Network Terminal in your hand. Tap a Network Core with it, then use it anywhere in that dimension: search, take items, or deposit your inventory. The Deepcore Portable Terminal reaches the core from any dimension.

Portable Terminal:
1: Steel Plate | Ender Pearl | Steel Plate
2: Steel Plate | Network Terminal | Steel Plate
3: Steel Plate | Redstone Dust | Steel Plate
Deepcore Portable Terminal:
1: Deepcore Alloy Plate | Eye of Ender | Deepcore Alloy Plate
2: Deepcore Alloy Plate | Portable Terminal | Deepcore Alloy Plate
3: Deepcore Alloy Plate | Elite Circuit | Deepcore Alloy Plate

entries.name: Dust
entries.summary: Iron, Gold and Copper Dust, 2 per ore from the Crusher.

blocks.html: Iron, Gold and Copper Dust, 2 per ore from the Crusher.
Smelt it into an ingot, or send it to the Washer for more.
Not crafted: see the entries above for the machine that makes it.

entries.name: Clean Dust
entries.summary: Made by the Washer. Smelts into an ingot, or goes on to the Purifier.

blocks.html: Made by the Washer. Smelts into an ingot, or goes on to the Purifier.
Smelt it in this add-on's Electric Furnace or a normal furnace.
Not crafted: see the entries above for the machine that makes it.

entries.name: Pure Dust
entries.summary: Made by the Purifier. The last stage: smelt it into an ingot.

blocks.html: Made by the Purifier. The last stage: smelt it into an ingot.
Per ore the chain gives 2, then 3, then 4 ingots.
Not crafted: see the entries above for the machine that makes it.

entries.name: Slag
entries.summary: A byproduct of the Washer (1 time in 10).

blocks.html: A byproduct of the Washer (1 time in 10).
Put it in the Sifter for small chances of nuggets and rare gems.
Not crafted: see the entries above for the machine that makes it.

categories.title: Gear
categories.blurb: Powered items you carry and wear, and how to charge them.

entries.name: Chargepad
entries.summary: Charges powered gear. Stand on it and everything you carry or wear that holds power fills up, up to 2,000 power a second, taken from the network it is cabled to (generators…

blocks.html: Charges powered gear. Stand on it and everything you carry or wear that holds power fills up, up to 2,000 power a second, taken from the network it is cabled to (generators first, batteries last). The front lamp and top glow while it charges. Tap it to see what it is doing and how far it reaches.

It also charges the gear of players and Robits nearby, every 2 seconds: within 6 blocks, and each Range Chip adds 8 more (tap the pad with one; up to 3 chips for 30 blocks). Power is lost on the way: 2% for every block away (12% at 6 blocks, 60% at 30). Standing on the pad loses nothing. The 2,000 a second limit counts the power it takes, losses included. Mining the pad gives its chips back.

entries.name: Jetpack
entries.summary: Wear it in the chest slot. Hold jump to climb, let go to glide down slowly, sneak to drop. It holds 40,000 power: about 2.5 minutes of climbing, and gliding costs almost…

blocks.html: Wear it in the chest slot. Hold jump to climb, let go to glide down slowly, sneak to drop. It holds 40,000 power: about 2.5 minutes of climbing, and gliding costs almost nothing. It warns you at 10% and when empty, and you glide down instead of falling. Charge it on a Chargepad. Its charge shows on the item.
Climbs faster, holds 80,000 and can hover: hold the Pipe Wrench, use it in the air and switch Hover on, and you hold your height when you let go of jump (40 power a second).
Server admins: /scriptevent dq:jetpacks off (or on) switches jetpacks off for everyone.

Deepcore Jetpack:
1: Deepcore Alloy Plate | Elite Circuit | Deepcore Alloy Plate
2: Deepcore Alloy Plate | Jetpack | Deepcore Alloy Plate
3: Blaze Rod | (empty) | Blaze Rod

entries.name: Deepcore Drill
entries.summary: A powered pickaxe, shovel and axe in one. It holds 60,000 power and uses about 40 a block (60 for ore). Use it in the air to switch mode, sneak + use for its settings.

blocks.html:
A powered pickaxe, shovel and axe in one. It holds 60,000 power and uses about 40 a block (60 for ore). Use it in the air to switch mode, sneak + use for its settings.
Fast: one block, quickly.
Vein: the whole ore vein or tree, up to 64 blocks (128 for the Mk II).
Tunnel: 3 x 3 facing the way you look (5 x 5 for the Mk II).
Gentle: silk touch.

It takes the quarry's chips: Fortune (up to 3), Silk Touch and Magnet (drops go straight into your inventory). Open its settings and press Install chips you carry; Take chips out gives them back. Fortune and Silk Touch don't mix. Blocks break the way a quarry breaks them, and ore gives its XP. Machines, chests and other add-on blocks break the normal way (one at a time).

Mk II:
1: (empty) | Diamond Drill Head | (empty)
2: Deepcore Alloy Plate | Elite Circuit | Deepcore Alloy Plate
3: Deepcore Alloy Plate | Deepcore Drill | Deepcore Alloy Plate

entries.name: Machine sides
entries.summary: Every face of a machine can be set with the Pipe Wrench:

blocks.html:
Every face of a machine can be set with the Pipe Wrench:
Both (the default): items go in and out.
In only: pipes and chests on that face can feed it, but it never pushes out there and pipes cannot pull from it there.
Out only: it pushes out there, but nothing is put in there.
Closed: nothing goes in or out.

Tap a machine face that has no pipe with the wrench to step through the modes. Tap its front to turn the machine a quarter turn instead. On a face with a pipe, the pipe's wrench form has the machine side at the bottom. Holding the wrench and looking at a machine shows its set sides with small particles. Sides are world directions (East, West, Up, Down, South, North), the same names the pipe sides use.

entries.name: Mining Suit
entries.summary: Four powered armour pieces (as tough as diamond, they never wear out). Each holds 100,000 power and takes modules; a Chargepad charges everything you wear. Modules only work…

blocks.html: Four powered armour pieces (as tough as diamond, they never wear out). Each holds 100,000 power and takes modules; a Chargepad charges everything you wear. Modules only work while their piece has power, and it warns you when one runs out.

Use a module in the air while wearing its piece to install it. Use the Pipe Wrench in the air to switch modules on and off or take them all out.
Helmet: Night Vision (5 power a second), Ore Sense (sneak: every ore within 8 blocks glows in its colour, 150 power a look).
Chestplate: Jetpack (flies like the Deepcore Jetpack, hover too, from the chestplate's charge), Shield (40% less damage, 8 a second plus 150 per point of damage).
Leggings: Speed (Speed II, 6 a second), Fire Protection (no damage from fire, lava, magma or burning. 2 power a second standing by; while the heat is on you it costs 40 a second on fire, 50 on magma, 100 in fire, 200 in soul fire, 500 in lava).
Boots: Fall Protection (no fall damage, 100 a fall).

Helmet: Hardened Steel Plate | Advanced Circuit | Hardened Steel Plate, then Hardened Steel Plate | Glass | Hardened Steel Plate.
Chestplate: Hardened Steel Plate | (empty) | Hardened Steel Plate, Hardened Steel Plate | Diamond Battery Bank | Hardened Steel Plate, Hardened Steel Plate | Advanced Circuit | Hardened Steel Plate.
Leggings: Hardened Steel Plate | Advanced Circuit | Hardened Steel Plate, then two rows of Hardened Steel Plate | (empty) | Hardened Steel Plate.
Boots: Hardened Steel Plate | (empty) | Hardened Steel Plate, then Hardened Steel Plate | Advanced Circuit | Hardened Steel Plate.

entries.summary: Every module is made the same way, rows from the top:

blocks.title: Suit modules
blocks.note: Every module is made the same way

blocks.html:
Night Vision: Golden Carrot
Ore Sense: Compass
Shield: Shield
Speed: Sugar

Fire Protection: Magma Cream

entries.name: Teleporter Pad
entries.summary: Stand on a pad and sneak: a list of the other pads opens. Pick one and you are there. Tap a pad with an empty hand to give it a name.

blocks.html: Stand on a pad and sneak: a list of the other pads opens. Pick one and you are there. Tap a pad with an empty hand to give it a name.

A Teleporter Pad reaches pads in its own dimension. A Deepcore Teleporter Pad reaches every pad, in the Overworld, the Nether and the End. The pad you leave from pays, from its network: 2,000 power plus 10 a block, or 10,000 to another dimension. The pad glows while someone stands on it.

blocks.html: A little robot helper. Use the Robit item on the ground to put it down; it is yours and follows you (it catches up if you get far away, even in another dimension). It cannot be hurt.
Tap it to open its 27 slots. Sneak + tap for its settings:

Magnet: picks up items within 6 blocks into its slots (10 power a stack).
Smelting: smelts what it carries, one a second, like the Electric Furnace (100 power each).
Pick up: back into a Robit item, keeping its charge (what it carries drops).
It holds 50,000 power. Stand it on a Chargepad (tell it to Stay there) to charge it. Only its owner can open it.

1: Steel Plate | Advanced Circuit | Steel Plate
2: Furnace | Steel Machine Casing | Chest
3: Steel Plate | Copper Coil | Steel Plate

blocks.html: A world of its own for mining: grass hills over solid stone, deepslate below 0 and bedrock at -64, with about twice the ores of the Overworld (coal, iron, copper, gold, redstone, lapis, diamond, emerald). No trees, water, villages or caves, and no mobs: any that appear are removed. Pets and named mobs you bring are left alone.
Bedrock has one clock for every world, so the sun still sets there; instead everyone in the Mining World gets Night Vision (no particles) the whole time they are there.
The land is made as you explore, a chunk at a time, so the edge can look empty for a moment. Quarries, machines and Teleporter Pads all work there (a Deepcore Teleporter Pad reaches it too).
Needs Bedrock 26.30 or newer on every player and the server.

blocks.html: Build a rectangle of Portal Frames standing up (like a Nether portal) round an empty space at least 2 wide and 3 tall, at most 21 x 21. The corners are optional. Then use a Portal Core on any frame: the portal lights (the core is used up) and a matching lit portal is built in the Mining World at the same X and Z, on the ground with a little clearing.

Stand in a portal for 2 seconds to go through. Light one in the Mining World and its partner is built in the Overworld. A portal links to the nearest lit portal within 16 blocks of the matching spot, like Nether portals; if there is none, a new one is built when you go through.
Break any frame (or the portal) and it goes out. Light it again with another core.

Portal Frame (makes 4):
1: Steel Plate | Iron Ingot | Steel Plate
2: Iron Ingot | Obsidian | Iron Ingot
3: Steel Plate | Iron Ingot | Steel Plate
Portal Core:
1: Steel Plate | Ender Pearl | Steel Plate
2: Amethyst Shard | Advanced Circuit | Amethyst Shard
3: Steel Plate | Ender Pearl | Steel Plate
The Assembler makes both for half.
